parameters.name: column1
parameters.description: One end of an existing inactive relationship in the model.
parameters.examNote: The relationship must already exist in the model as inactive. USERELATIONSHIP cannot create new relationships.

parameters.name: column2
parameters.description: The other end of the same inactive relationship.
parameters.examNote: Column order does not matter — either column can be listed first.

returnType: Used only as a filter argument inside CALCULATE — does not return a value
summary: USERELATIONSHIP temporarily activates an inactive relationship for the scope of a CALCULATE expression. Essential for role-playing dimensions where multiple date relationships exist (OrderDate, ShipDate, DeliveryDate all joined to the same DimDate table).

examples.label: Filter Sales by Ship Date instead of Order Date
examples.expression:
Shipped Sales =
CALCULATE(
  SUM(Sales[Amount]),
  USERELATIONSHIP(Sales[ShipDate], DimDate[Date])
)
examples.explanation: The active relationship is Sales[OrderDate]→DimDate. USERELATIONSHIP temporarily deactivates it and activates Sales[ShipDate]→DimDate. Date slicers now filter by ShipDate for this measure only.

steps: Model has two relationships: active Sales[OrderDate]→DimDate, inactive Sales[ShipDate]→DimDate
USERELATIONSHIP deactivates the OrderDate relationship for this CALCULATE scope
The ShipDate relationship becomes active within this scope
Date slicers now filter Sales rows by ShipDate instead of OrderDate

commonTraps: USERELATIONSHIP can only activate an EXISTING inactive relationship — you cannot reference columns that have no defined relationship.
USERELATIONSHIP must be placed inside CALCULATE as a filter argument — it cannot be used standalone.
Only one relationship between the same two tables can be active at a time.
